notes: Third sweep at 0397dec, skill condition: five runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. Every transcript reads SKILL.md, references/testing.md and references/processes.md (opus-1 with cat in Bash, the others with Read), matching reads in result.json; no Skill tool call. Expected reads is met in 5 of 5; in the previous sweep both haiku runs missed processes.md.

One graded rule changed since db91c23: "Assert with patterns" in references/testing.md gained the sentence that now decides it: "A value the test already holds goes into the pattern with the pin operator, `^subscriber`, or the whole value is compared with `==`; a match that binds the value and an `==` on it afterwards is the shape to replace.", with the example assert [pid] = Subscriptions.subscribers(server, "news") / assert pid == self(). 0 of 5 runs violate: every run compares subscriber lists whole with == (e.g. opus-1 line 37, haiku-1 line 90, haiku-2 line 99, sonnet-1 line 128 with a setup-bound survivor, sonnet-2 line 46) and pins held values in :DOWN patterns. Previous sweep: 2 of 5 skill runs (both sonnet) violated with that exact shape.

The other six graded rules are unchanged since db91c23 and graded to the 2026-10-22 standard. "Group tests by function and name them by behaviour" is violated in 2 of 5 runs, both on test names, none on blocks: haiku-1 line 34: test "returns :ok" (the rule's own example) and sonnet-2 line 117: test "succeeds when the topic has no subscribers". The sonnet-2 verdict is a judgment: its body only asserts the :ok return and an empty list, and the previous baseline grade counted "returns :ok even with no subscribers" as this violation; reading "succeeds" as a behaviour instead would make sonnet-2 and the Sonnet tier clean on this rule. haiku-2 line 82 and sonnet-1 line 118 ("does nothing ...") were graded clean. No run has a describe block joining two functions; all five use a condition block named "when a subscribed process exits"/"has exited", three with a named or inline setup.

"Start processes with `start_supervised!/1`": 0 of 5 violate. All five name every server Module.concat(module, test); only sonnet-1 tests a failing start, with start_supervised/1 matching the KeyError reason (lines 42-45) under a separate test-specific name (line 40). No start_link call from any test. Subscriber helper processes are started with start_supervised! in opus-1 (Task) and sonnet-2 (temporary Agent), and with spawn/spawn_monitor/spawn_link in haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1, which the previous sweep graded clean. Previous sweep: 1 of 5 (haiku-1, GenServer.start/2).

"Run tests concurrently unless they share global state": 0 of 5 violate; all use async: true with a Registry started in setup_all and keyed by Module.concat(module, test). "Wait for messages, not for time": 0 of 5; every exit test waits for its own :DOWN monitor (sonnet-1 adds :sys.get_state), refutes follow a sync call or use refute_receive, and no file contains Process.sleep or polls Process.alive?. "Replace dependencies at boundaries, through behaviours" and "Use setup for shared data" are clean in 5 of 5.

SKILL.md rules changed since db91c23 (one-step with, the new do: rule, captures) are outside this case's list; I checked the files for them and found nothing to report (the only do: bodies are accessors or one-call helpers, e.g. sonnet-1 line 9: def registry, do: @registry and haiku-2 line 163: defp sync(server), do: :sys.get_state(server)). other_violations is empty in all five runs.

Tests were run from copies in the scratch folder with elixir -r test-writing-input.ex subscriptions_test.exs on Elixir 1.20.4, 20 times each with random seeds; every run passed every time with no compiler warnings (opus-1 12 tests, haiku-1 13, haiku-2 12, sonnet-1 12, sonnet-2 14). All five pass mix format --check-formatted, confirming format_ok in result.json.
